question.worked_solution:
We first write $288a$ as the product $144\cdot 2a$ which contains a perfect square $(144):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{288a} & = \\ \sqrt{144\cdot 2a} & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can separate the product into two separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{144\cdot 2a} & = \\ \sqrt{(12)^{2}\cdot 2a} & = \\ \sqrt{(12)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2a} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify the radical containing the perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(12)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ |12|\cdot \sqrt{2a} & = \\ 12\sqrt{2a} & \end{aligned}
$$
